note: The compliance gate for a real fintech account. Edit this, not the code: the person who owns the account's risk owns this file. Patterns are Python regexes, case-insensitive. Levels: blocked_patterns refuses to publish, required_context adds a disclosure, escalate_topics sends the conversation to a human.

blocked_patterns.why: Promising an outcome on a financial product is a regulatory problem, not a copy problem.
A stated periodic return reads as a performance promise regardless of intent.
Multiplier claims are the classic pump language.

blocked_patterns.pattern: \b(you should|i suggest you|my advice to you|buy this now|sell now|you must buy|book profit now)\b
blocked_patterns.why: Personalised buy/sell instruction on an educational account is unregistered advice.
Never claim a registration you do not hold. Put the real number in brand/credentials.json or cut the line.
Profit screenshots presented as proof imply repeatability. Show method, not wins.
Manufactured urgency about markets is both a compliance and a trust problem.
A price-level instruction is advice about a security, not education.

required_context.add: Educational content, not investment advice. Markets carry risk of loss.

disclosure_footer: Educational content only. Not investment advice. Markets carry risk of loss.
regulated_notes: India: SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations require registration to give advice on securities for consideration. Educational content is the line this account walks.
Profit claims about trading are 'past performance' claims under the SEBI ad code; they cannot be presented as indicative of future results.
US: FTC endorses the 'results not typical' rule for income claims; SEC Rule 206(4)-1 covers testimonials by advisers.
Always name the risk, never the return. That is the whole rule.
